newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-PARTIES TO TELL SHKELE READY TO QUIT GOVERNMENT.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-PARTIES TO TELL SHKELE READY TO QUIT GOVERNMENT.

text.p: The leading government parties are ready inform Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Friday that they intend to discuss leaving the government, politicians said.
Democratic Party Saimnieks (DPS), Latvia's Way, Fatherland and Freedom and the Farmers' Union have agreed to discuss the possibility of leaving the seven-party coalition government.
"The heads of parties and factions will inform Shkele that they will ask their respective decision-making bodies to consider leaving the government," a DPS spokesman told Reuters.
"The (political) situation shows that the prime minister is placing himself above the government declaration and any failure is explained by internal party bickering," the spokesman said.
The parties have set meetings this week and early next week to decide on the issue.
An extraordinary conference by second-largest party Latvia's Way and the DPS council are to set to meet on August 4 while the Fatherland and Freedom board will convene later toady.
The government has been plagued by ministerial resignatinos amid anti-corruption scandals and rows between Shkele and the parties.
Shkele was asked to become prime minister in late 1995 after two failed attempts to find a prime minister from one of the political parties after inconclusive elections in October.
